As of 310 PM EDT Wednesday...

KEY MESSAGE 1...Very warm, record breaking temperatures this 
afternoon quickly give way to increasing clouds and a much 
cooler day Thursday.

Latest surface analysis reveals ~1020 mb surface high pressure
centered over the western Atlantic. To the north, a wavy front
remains draped over the northern mid-Atlantic into New England.
To the west, a chilly 1024+ mb high is centered over the
Northern Plains, and will push into the Upper Midwest by this
evening. Aloft, an upper ridge centered over the west-central
Gulf coast extends into the local area. The rising heights are
allowing unseasonable warmth across the region. Upstream, a
closed low over the Four Corners region will be absorbed into a
northern stream trough which will drop across the Canadian
Prairies tonight into tomorrow. It is this system which will
bring sharply colder air to the region this weekend. 

Locally, temperatures are well into the 80s to around 90 at 19z.
Several local records for the date have already been broken.
These have been included below for reference.

High pressure to the north will slowly build across the Great
Lakes and New England tonight and early Thursday, slowly pushing
the front to the north closer to the area. That front will
cross into the region Thu morning. Clouds will increase
overnight, with mostly cloudy conditions then persisting through
tomorrow evening. A few showers could accompany the front as it
pushes into the area late tonight, but the frontal passage
should be mainly dry.

The surface high ridges down the eastern slope of the
Appalachians Thursday, allowing a CAD wedge to develop. High-res
guidance continues to trend cooler for tomorrow and highs have
been nudged slightly down given the persistent overcast
conditions and chilly NE flow. Weak isentropic lift across the
northern zones will primarily reinforce the developing stratus,
it could also allow for some light sprinkles or light rain
tomorrow morning. Highs near and south of the VA/NC line will
rise back into the 70s to near 80 with clouds being a bit
thinner and slower to arrive. Farther north, especially N of
I-64, temperatures will follow a non-diurnal temperature curve
with highs realized in the morning or by midday before leveling
off or even falling off slightly.

KEY MESSAGE 2...Warm and breezy Friday with a few gusty showers
Friday night into Saturday. Much cooler temperatures arrive 
this weekend.

The Canadian deep upper trough is forecast to dig across the 
Great Lakes Thursday night into Friday with a strengthening 
surface low over the Ohio Valley. Southerly flow ahead of this 
feature will allow the front to lift back northward as a warm 
front Friday morning. High temps rebound into the low 80s N with
mid and upper 80s S. It will become breezy out of the SW by 
Friday afternoon. A rapidly deepening low pressure will 
translate NE into New England on Friday with a strong cold front
extending back to the southwest. This front will cross the 
local area late Friday evening into early Saturday with 
significant cold advection moving into the region. Trends from
the past few cycles of probabilistic guidance, along with the 
ECMWF/CMC deterministic runs are favoring a stronger shortwave
trough which digs farther south into the mid-Atlantic. This
results in a slightly slower progression of the front late
Friday night and Saturday. While QPF remains light steep low- 
level lapse rates and vigorous momentum transfer could mix down 
35-40 mph gusts to the surface fairly easily coincident with the
frontal passage. Otherwise, while favorable kinematics support 
storm organization, meager moisture/instability and now later 
nocturnal timing all significantly limit severe potential beyond
the previously referenced gusty frontal wind threat.

Strong (1035mb+) high pressure builds into the region behind the 
front with upper troughing remaining over the eastern CONUS, 
resulting in well below normal temperatures this weekend. Given
the delayed timing and subsequent onset of cold advection, Sat
highs are also likely to be realized early in the day. Afternoon
temps likely remain more or less steady even with gradual
clearing, with upper 50s to low 60s S/SE. It will also remain 
quite breezy on Saturday with gusts 25-30 mph, and especially 
near the coast where winds could gust 30-35 mph. Overnight low 
temps tumble into the mid to upper 30s in the Piedmont with low 
to mid 40s for the remainder of the area Saturday night. Upper 
30s and low 40s are forecast Sunday night into Monday. Some 
frost is possible in the Piedmont with this airmass, especially 
if temps continue to trend toward the cooler MOS guidance which 
shows temps in the low 30s in the typically cooler spots.
